newsitem.title: USA: NHL committee selects four cities for expansion.
newsitem.headline: NHL committee selects four cities for expansion.

text.p: The National Hockey League's expansion committee Tuesday recommended awarding new franchises to groups in Atlanta, Nashville, Minneapolis-St. Paul and Columbus, Ohio.
The committee recommended that a Nashville franchise begin play in 1998, Atlanta in 1999, the St. Paul-based franchise in 2000 and Columbus in 2000.

The recommendations next go before the NHL's ruling board of governors for approval at its June 25 meeting, the league said. A three-fourths vote of league owners is required for admission of new franchises.
Nashville already has an arena ready for a new franchise, but the three other expansion bids include the construction of partly bond-financed arenas.
A $213 million Atlanta arena would rely in part on $140 million of revenue bonds.

St. Paul has committed to $30 million of bonds for a new $130 million arena and pledged to issue another $65 million of debt if Minnesota lawmakers choose not to include it in a capital spending bill next year.
Columbus has approved private financing for a $125 million arena that would include more than $20 million of infrastructure improvements paid by the city and Franklin County.
The Nashville franchise would be majority-owned by Leipold Hockey Holdings LLC, jointly held by Craig Leipold and the S.C. Johnson family, the league noted.
Turner Broadcasting System Inc, owner of the Atlanta Hawks basketball team, is the bidder for the Atlanta hockey franchise.

The Columbus team is expected to be owned by a group led by Worthington Industries Chairman John McConnell and the Minneapolis-St. Paul franchise would be a limited partnership led by billboard magnate Robert Naegele Jr.
The expansion committee also considered bids from Houston and Oklahoma City groups. Each ownership group must pay an $80 million franchise fee.
